title.en: What decides the form of a market

body.en: *Markets* are classified by the number of buyers and sellers, the nature of the product (identical or differentiated), freedom of entry and exit, knowledge of the market, and the control a firm has over price. Perfect competition has a very large number of firms selling an identical product with free entry, so each firm is a price taker. A monopoly is a single seller of a product with no close substitutes, protected by barriers to entry; it is a price maker.

points.en: Perfect competition: many firms, homogeneous product, free entry, price taker
Monopoly: one seller, no close substitutes, strong barriers, price maker

title.en: On the board: Comparing market forms

say.en: Compare the four forms on their main features.
Oligopoly sits between them: a few large, interdependent firms.

text.en: Oligopoly: few firms, interdependence, rivals react

say.en: On the board: Comparing market forms.

body.en: *Monopolistic competition* has many firms selling differentiated products (brands of soap or toothpaste) with fairly free entry; each firm has a little control over price and spends on advertising and other selling costs. Oligopoly has a few large firms selling identical or differentiated products; because each is large, the firms are interdependent: one firm's price change provokes reactions from rivals, so demand is uncertain. Under perfect competition AR = MR is a horizontal line; in the other forms AR slopes down and MR lies below it.

points.en: *Monopolistic competition*: product differentiation, selling costs, elastic AR
*Oligopoly*: few firms, interdependence, barriers, price rigidity
AR slopes down whenever the firm has some control over price

problem.en: A firm finds that it can sell 100 units at ₹20 and 120 units at ₹18. Another firm can sell any quantity at ₹20 but nothing above it. Identify the market forms.

steps.en: The first firm must lower its price to sell more: its AR curve slopes down, so it has some control over price.
This fits monopolistic competition (or monopoly or oligopoly).
The second firm faces a horizontal AR at ₹20: it is a price taker.

answer.en: First firm: imperfect competition (downward AR). Second firm: perfect competition (horizontal AR).

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. A firm finds that it can sell 100 units at 20 rupees and 120 units at 18 rupees. Another firm can sell any quantity at 20 rupees but nothing above it. Identify the market forms.
The first firm must lower its price to sell more: its AR curve slopes down, so it has some control over price.
This fits monopolistic competition or monopoly or oligopoly.
The second firm faces a horizontal AR at 20 rupees: it is a price taker.
That is perfect competition.
So the answer is First firm: imperfect competition downward AR. Second firm: perfect competition horizontal AR.
